Rates of trait evolution from the turnover of partners in a metacommunity

Source: R/traits_rates.R
turnover_rates.Rd

Turns the turnover of interaction partners of each species in a simulated metacommunity, from partner_turnover(), into rates of evolution of a continuous trait on the branches of its tree, for trait_rates(edge_rates = ). It implements the expectation that evolution speeds up with each change in the community around a lineage and stays slow while the community is stable (McPeek 2017; scenario 5 of the notes on branch rates).

Usage

turnover_rates(
  x,
  tree = x$tree,
  sigma2 = 1,
  k = 1,
  window = NULL,
  partners = c("all", "competitors")
)

Arguments

x

An mc_sim object with history, that is, run with record_steps.

tree

The tree of the species in x; by default the one stored in x.

sigma2

Rate outside the stretch informed by the metacommunity.

k

Increase of the rate, relative to sigma2, per unit of turnover (partners gained or lost per site and time step).

window

Length of the end of each tip branch represented by the metacommunity, in the units of the branch lengths; NULL uses the whole tip branch. A window longer than a tip branch is cut to its length.

partners

"all" counts every other species as a partner; "competitors" counts only the species with a non-zero competition coefficient with the focal species in x$alpha (in either direction).

Value

Numeric vector with the rate of each branch, in the order of the rows of tree$edge, with the turnover of each species as attribute "turnover".

Details

The metacommunity runs in ecological time among the species at the tips, so its dynamics only inform the tip branches, and how ecological time relates to branch lengths is a choice of the user, not something the simulation gives. Here the dynamics are taken to represent the last window units of time of each tip branch: in that stretch the rate is \(\mathrm{sigma2}\, (1 + k \cdot \mathrm{turnover})\), and elsewhere, including all internal branches, it is sigma2. The rate of a tip branch is the mean over the branch, weighted by time.

References

McPeek, M. A. (2017). Evolutionary Community Ecology. Princeton University Press. doi:10.23943/princeton/9780691088778.001.0001

See also

partner_turnover(), history_rates(), trait_rates()

Other species traits: arrival_ages(), as_herodotools(), food_web_rates(), history_rates(), paint_regimes(), partner_turnover(), plot.rate_matrix(), plot_rates(), plot_traits(), rate_matrix(), region_pool(), species_traits(), tip_history_metrics(), trait_bm(), trait_mk(), trait_ou(), trait_rates()

Examples

set.seed(1)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(10)
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(landscape_implicit(15), species_traits(tr),
                              competition_matrix(tr, "none"), n_steps = 300,
                              record_steps = seq(100, 300, 20), extirpation = 0.02)
rates <- turnover_rates(sim, k = 20, window = 0.1)
x <- trait_rates(tr, edge_rates = rates)
